[01:14] That's what interoperability solves. You architect the data layer so that information flows consistently and securely across all these different systems. And here's the thing, this is not a one-time project. It's an ongoing practice. So, here are three practices that matter. First, semantic organization.

[01:40] Define common terms. So like customer should mean the same thing across all of your systems. Order status should mean the same thing and have consistent values. You're creating a shared vocabulary that agents can understand. Second, governed access. Just because an agent can access customer data doesn't mean that it should set permissions and audit access. Ensure compliance. If you're touching regulated data, you need to track it. Third, uh, real time or near realtime synchronization.

[02:20] If the agent reads from a data copy that's 3 days old, it will always give stale answers. You need systems that keep data fresh. So, those are your principles.
